o.text:
From Proto-Turkic *tün (“night, yesterday”)
Cognate with
Old Turkic 𐱅‬𐰇‬𐰤 (tün, “night, dark night”),
Turkish dün (“yesterday”),
Turkmen düýn (“yesterday”),
Crimean Tatar tünevin (“yesterday”) and dün (“yesterday”),
Karachay-Balkar тюнене (tünene, “yesterday”),
Uzbek tun (“night”),
Uyghur تۈن (tün, “dark”) and تۈنۈگۈن (tünügün, “yesterday”),
Tatar төн (tön, “night”),
Bashkir төн (tün, “night”),
Kazakh түн (tün, “night”) and
Kyrgyz түн (tün, “night”).

glosses: to skedaddle, to hightail, to flee

o.text:
Possibly from Proto-Turkic *yīr-, *yï̄r- (“to split lengthwise; to break, tear”), in which case a doublet of yırtmaq (“wear out; rend”). Compare with Crimean Tatar cırtmaq.
Alternatively, onomatopoeic.
From Persian ساخته کار. By surface analysis, saxta + -kar.
Borrowed from Russian филоло́гия (filológija), from French philologie.
